summary: Lincoln Parish Forestry Commission tower near Hilly, described by the federal survey in 1952 and manned daily in 1961; no source found on when or whether it came down.

Tower man for the Lincoln Parish unit; tower manned every day of the year
Sheriff said three men had apparently stolen a pulpwood truck, driven it to the Hilly Fire Tower and destroyed a hut used by on-duty rangers; three men arrested

corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page carries no status and no removal date, and the NGS datasheet lists only a 1952 observation. No source we read says the tower came down.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1952 survey description gives about 115 feet; a 1961 newspaper report quoted on the Forest Lookouts page gives 100 feet. The record's 30.5 m matches the 100-foot figure. The sources disagree, so the story reports both.
A March 1956 report calls the tower unused, while a 1961 report describes a tower man on duty every day. The sources do not show when staffing began, so no start date is given.

sources.title: NGS Datasheet for PID CQ2927 (Hilly Lookout Tower LFC)

notes_for_editor: The record's 'gone' status is not supported by the Forest Lookouts page, which has no status field, or by the NGS datasheet, which has no later history; it is proposed as 'unknown' above. The record's 30.5 m height is the 1961 figure; the 1952 survey says about 115 ft. Grokipedia describes the tower in the present tense with a 115-foot figure but cites nothing, so it was not used. The Wikipedia article on Hilly, Louisiana does not mention the tower. Coordinates in the record (32.6581, -92.6922) match the NGS mark within rounding. Trailmonger lists a 'Hilly Fire Tower Road' near Vienna, which shows only the road name. Anyplaceamerica returned 403. Useful next step: current aerial imagery at the NGS mark (32.65819, -92.69213) would settle whether anything stands. Used two web searches and four reads.
